title: 1H Budget swings to surplus; debt at 88.8% of GDP | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:45
-     - 0

President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake

The Government’s Budget swung to a surplus of Rs. 9.5 billion in the first half of 2026 from a deficit of Rs. 405.6 billion a year earlier, as a surge in revenue and lower execution of capital expenditure outpaced spending growth, while Government debt stood at Rs. 32 trillion, or 88.8% of estimated GDP.

This is according to the Finance, Planning and Economic Development’s Mid-Year Fiscal Position Report released yesterday under the Public Financial Management Act. It showed the primary surplus, which excludes interest payments, rising to Rs. 1.24 trillion from Rs. 859 billion, far above the end-June target of Rs. 72 billion under the IMF Extended Fund Facility (EFF).

1H...

Total revenue rose 27.2% to Rs. 2.95 trillion, or 56.1% of the annual estimate. Tax revenue grew 25.9% to Rs. 2.71 trillion, driven largely by a 255.7% jump in vehicle imports to 313,480 units, which more than doubled Excise Duty on motor vehicles to Rs. 266.4 billion and lifted Customs Import Duty by 63.6% to Rs. 153.7 billion.

VAT rose 25.4% to Rs. 987.6 billion and income tax 16.3% to Rs. 568.4 billion. 

“Sri Lanka Customs and the Inland Revenue Department were the main contributors to the increase in tax revenue, reflecting stronger collections from both import-related and domestic taxes,” the report said. The direct to indirect tax ratio, however, shifted to 21:79 from 23:77.

Expenditure grew a slower 7.9% to Rs. 2.95 trillion. Interest payments fell 2.4% to Rs. 1.23 trillion, while salaries rose 12% to Rs. 621.7 billion on public sector pay revisions and welfare spending reached Rs. 550.8 billion. 

Capital expenditure and net lending rose 23.6% to Rs. 276.6 billion but amounted to only 16.1% of the annual estimate of Rs. 1.72 trillion. “This outcome may be attributed to the phased implementation of development projects and the prioritization of public investment expenditure,” the Ministry said of lower-than-estimated capital payments.

Of the total debt stock at end-June, external debt amounted to $ 38 billion, comprising multilateral (39%), commercial (33%) and bilateral (28%) debt, while domestic debt stood at Rs. 19.2 trillion, 84% of it in Treasury Bonds. About 82% of borrowing in the first half was raised domestically, mainly through Treasury Bonds, while net Treasury Bill issuance was negative at Rs. 720.9 billion. “The reduction in Treasury Bill issuance also indicates a shift away from short-term financing,” the report said.

Debt service, excluding Treasury Bill maturities, totalled Rs. 2.32 trillion, of which Rs. 1.2 trillion was interest. External debt service amounted to $ 1.25 billion, and there were no external payment arrears at end-June.

Agreements covering 93% of the bilateral debt to be restructured had been concluded by 30 June, with the remainder expected by end-2026, while talks with creditors from 13 countries are ongoing. “Following the successful finalization of loan agreements, Sri Lanka has resumed regular debt servicing to the respective creditor partners,” the Ministry said.

Outstanding Treasury guarantees and letters of comfort stood at Rs. 971.2 billion at end-March, 51.3% of them in foreign currency.

title: SOE profits rise in 1H, SriLankan losses deepen | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:45
-     - 1

The Finance Ministry yesterday said 51 major State Owned Enterprises (SOEs) reported a combined profit of Rs. 259.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up from Rs. 227.8 billion a year earlier.

The rise in cumulative earnings is despite rising input costs, supply chain disruptions and order cancellations caused by the Middle East conflict, with State banks leading the gains while Treasury subsidies supported Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) and SriLankan Airlines sank deeper into losses.

The figures are contained in the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development’s Mid-Year Fiscal Position Report released yesterday. Between April and June, the General Treasury provided subsidies of Rs. 41 billion to the CPC and Rs. 15 billion to the National System Operator (Private) Limited (NSO) to mitigate the impact of the conflict on the public and the wider economy.

The State banks delivered the strongest results. Bank of Ceylon (BoC) reported profit before tax (PBT) of Rs. 62.6 billion, up from Rs. 59.4 billion, driven by a 9.2% rise in total operating income to Rs. 131.4 billion. Its loans and advances grew 6.6% to Rs. 2.5 trillion while deposits fell 1.6% to Rs. 4.3 trillion, and its impaired (Stage III) loans ratio, a measure of bad loans, improved to 5.01% from 5.59% at end-2025. People’s Bank recorded an all-time high PBT of Rs. 32.6 billion against Rs. 28 billion, on an 18.9% rise in net interest income to Rs. 82.4 billion, with loans up 9.7% to Rs. 1.9 trillion, deposits down 2% to Rs. 3.2 trillion and its Stage III ratio improving to 6.7% from 7.7%. National Savings Bank’s PBT fell 6.2% to Rs. 22.6 billion, mainly due to a 10% rise in personnel expenses to Rs. 13.8 billion.

The CPC’s results reflected the conflict’s direct cost. Net sales revenue rose 40.4% to Rs. 576.6 billion on higher domestic fuel prices, but its petroleum import bill surged 73.8% to $ 1.7 billion from $ 1 billion amid disruptions to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and higher shipping and insurance costs. Cost of sales rose 50.2% to Rs. 567.6 billion, cutting gross profit by 72.9% to Rs. 8.9 billion. Operating profit nevertheless rose to Rs. 23.9 billion from Rs. 11.1 billion, mainly due to the April to June subsidy, and with an unrealised exchange gain of Rs. 7.2 billion, net profit rose 71.8% to Rs. 29.2 billion. Total fuel subsidies to domestic petroleum market players amounted to about Rs. 57 billion.

SriLankan Airlines posted a loss before tax of Rs. 35.6 billion in the first quarter of the 2026/27 financial year, against Rs. 12 billion a year earlier, based on unaudited management accounts. Revenue rose to Rs. 82.8 billion from Rs. 62.6 billion, but total expenditure climbed 40.4% to Rs. 95.2 billion as aircraft fuel costs jumped about 93% to Rs. 41.2 billion, producing an operating loss of about Rs. 12.5 billion before exchange losses. The group’s net loss narrowed to Rs. 32.2 billion after Rs. 3.4 billion in net income from SriLankan Catering.

“The above financial performance demonstrates that SLA continues to face significant structural financial and liquidity challenges,” the report said. With total liabilities of Rs. 561.4 billion against assets of Rs. 209.9 billion, the airline reported negative equity of Rs. 351.5 billion at end-June. “This is particularly significant given the Company’s existing debt burden and the continuing requirement for Government support to ensure uninterrupted operations,” the Ministry said.

That support continued in the first half. The Government serviced instalments on selected BoC and People’s Bank loans to the airline, released $ 30 million for short-term funding needs and absorbed $ 126.5 million in restructured guaranteed Bonds into the Government debt stock from 20 March, 2026. In June, the Cabinet approved a Strategy and Restructuring Committee to undertake a comprehensive review of the airline.

In the power sector, the Ceylon Electricity Board’s (CEB) functions passed to six wholly government-owned successor companies from 9 March, 2026 under the Sri Lanka Electricity Act. The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) approved an average 10.3% tariff increase in April and a further 18% increase in May for selected categories, including domestic consumers using more than 180 units a month and all Government entities, while the Rs. 15 billion NSO subsidy supported the remaining categories, about 95% of consumers. Electricity sales revenue rose 20% to Rs. 231.2 billion as demand grew about 7% to 9,304 GWh and average revenue per unit rose to Rs. 31.9 per kWh from Rs. 24.6. Hydropower generation fell about 23%, and despite a 57% rise in rooftop solar, thermal fuel generation increased about 88% to meet demand. The Treasury also provided Rs. 8 billion in equity to fund a Voluntary Retirement Scheme for CEB employees who did not move to the successor companies.

Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) lifted profit 19% to Rs. 29.1 billion, helped by a 9% rise in operational revenue to Rs. 44.1 billion and a foreign exchange gain of Rs. 2.7 billion, although containerised cargo fell 6% to 1.2 million TEUs. “The decline in containerized cargo volumes and the changing global shipping environment remain areas requiring close monitoring to sustain the Authority’s financial performance,” the report said.

Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) (Private) Limited (AASL) more than doubled PBT to Rs. 24.9 billion from Rs. 11.2 billion, on a 17% rise in non-aeronautical revenue to Rs. 23.4 billion and an exchange gain of Rs. 5.6 billion against a loss of Rs. 4.3 billion a year earlier, as aircraft diversions to Sri Lanka offset flight cancellations, including 115 at Bandaranaike International Airport in a single day. “The continuing uncertainty in the Middle East, particularly its potential impact on flight connectivity and passenger movements, warrants close monitoring given the importance of Middle Eastern routes to Sri Lanka’s aviation and tourism sectors,” the Ministry said.

Elsewhere, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board’s net profit fell 8.5% to Rs. 16.2 billion as higher pumping costs lifted cost of sales about 10%, while non-revenue water edged up to 24.4%. Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation Limited raised PBT 10.3% to Rs. 2.6 billion.

On restructuring, a dedicated SOE restructuring unit set up under the Ministry in March 2026 is liquidating 33 selected SOEs, while the Treasury had settled Rs. 2.8 billion of the Rs. 5 billion allocated in the 2026 Budget for long-outstanding Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Trust Fund (ETF) and gratuity liabilities of selected SOEs by end-August.

title: With gains exhausted, Govt. must overhaul tax administration: IMF | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:44
-     - 3

Sri Lanka must move its revenue administration from a reactive, crisis-driven model to a modern, risk-based and digitally enabled one if the tax gains that doubled revenue to 15.4% of GDP since 2021 are to endure, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said, with the next phase of revenue mobilisation dependent on compliance, data and enforcement rather than higher tax rates.

The findings are contained in the IMF Fiscal Affairs Department’s (FAD) Revenue Administration Diagnostic, published by the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development on 30 October, 2026 in fulfilment of a structural benchmark, or reform commitment, under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF).

The report, based on a mission to Colombo from 24 June to 7 July, 2026 led by Andrew Kazora Okello, sets out the revenue administration pillar of a government-owned Medium-Term Revenue Strategy (MTRS).

The recovery from 7.3% of GDP in 2021 was led by VAT, which rose from 1.8% to 5.3% of GDP and accounted for about half the increase, while income tax rose from 1.9% to 3.5%. The IMF said, however, that the gains were made from a weak institutional base and against still-large compliance gaps, with risk-based methods emerging across the Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Sri Lanka Customs (SLC) and Sri Lanka Excise (SLE) but not yet consistently embedded in daily operations.

“In Sri Lanka’s case, the MTRS should be seen less as a vehicle for short-term tightening and more as a platform for locking in recent gains, updating the legal framework needed for modern administration, and moving from a reactive post-crisis model toward a more modern and trusted revenue system,” the report said. With the easier policy gains largely realised, the IMF said the strategy should not rely mainly on further statutory rate increases.

The data point to a deeper problem than late filing. In VAT, on-time filing improved between 2025 and the first quarter of 2026, from 80.1% to 85.7% for large taxpayers and from 45.9% to 55.9% for non-large taxpayers, yet non-filing rose from 12.3% to 19.1% among non-large taxpayers and from 0.3% to 4% among large ones. “These data suggest that recent compliance efforts have improved filing timeliness more than they have reduced non-filing, underscoring the need for stronger non-filer identification and follow-up,” the IMF said.

Income tax filing is weaker still. In 2025, non-filing reached 52.7% for corporate income tax (CIT), 45.6% for personal income tax (PIT) and 67.8% for individual income tax (IIT), with more taxpayers failing to file than filing on time in all three. The IMF traced this to weaknesses in non-filer detection, follow-up and enforcement credibility rather than the availability of electronic filing, and described Sri Lanka as a clear outlier with the weakest on-time filing across all major taxes among selected South Asian peers. “Sri Lanka’s results suggest that a large proportion of registered taxpayers are either failing to meet their filing obligations on time or have become inactive while remaining on the taxpayer register,” the report said.

That makes register cleanup central. VAT and CIT register cleanup is on track to meet the July 2026 structural benchmark, but IIT register cleansing can proceed only once adequate server capacity is available, given the volume of records involved.

The weakness extends to employer withholding. Of 47,662 employers required to file for 2025/26, on-time filing was 81% among those managed by the Large Taxpayer Office, but 38% among about 14,000 medium corporate taxpayers and 13% among some 27,600 employers managed by regional and metropolitan offices, which the IMF said reduces the IRD’s ability to detect under-withholding or non-remittance.

At the heart of the overhaul is compliance risk management (CRM), the practice of using data to direct audit, enforcement and service resources to the highest risks. VAT compliance improvement plans are in place, but risk registers, third-party data and analytics are not used consistently across tax types, the IMF said. “As a result, risk analysis does not yet consistently determine who is contacted, audited, assisted, or enforced against.” Penalties, though available in law, are not applied consistently.

The same gap shows in arrears. Tax defaults stood at about Rs. 2.1 trillion as at 31 December, 2025, compared with about Rs. 1.1 trillion in 2024, with about Rs. 1.6 trillion in dispute. “For debts not in dispute, continued aging points to staffing constraints, weak prioritization, and the absence of a risk-based framework to distinguish collectible debts from low-value, disputed, low-probability, or administratively uneconomic cases,” the report said. The IRD cannot write off bad debts without submission to the Ministry of Finance.

Systems are the most immediate risk. The maintenance contract for the Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS), the IRD’s core platform for registration, filing, payment, arrears, audit, refunds and taxpayer services, expires on 31 January, 2027, and the planned transition to a Sri Lanka-based support model has not begun. Foundational actions under the IRD’s IT Strategic Plan for 2025-2027, including data warehouse procurement and defining RAMIS 3.0 requirements, have also not progressed as envisaged. “Any interruption in vendor support, system maintenance, or operational troubleshooting could disrupt essential tax administration processes and put recent revenue gains at risk,” the IMF warned.

Administrative readiness should also set the pace of policy. Before lowering VAT thresholds or bringing materially more taxpayers into the system, the IRD should substantially improve register quality, digital filing and payment, taxpayer service and refund risk management, the IMF said.

If sustained, the overhaul could pay off. The IMF estimated that lifting Sri Lanka’s score on the Operational Strength Index (OSI), a measure of revenue administration capability, from 0.39 to 0.55 over five years could generate additional internal revenue of about 1.9 percentage points of GDP. It cautioned that the figure is illustrative, is not the MTRS revenue objective, excludes Customs, Excise and tax policy measures, and should not be treated as revenue additional to the baseline without further analysis.

Over the longer term, the report recommended considering a modern tax procedures code covering registration through to appeals and taxpayer rights, but cautioned against reaching for structural fixes first. “Options such as a revenue authority model, or other forms of closer structural integration, may merit consideration, but they should follow, and not substitute for, the operational, legal, and institutional foundations needed to make such reforms effective,” it said.

The IMF identified loss of momentum once the immediate crisis context fades as the principal implementation risk, and called for credible early wins, including cleaner taxpayer data, stronger filing and payment controls and more predictable treatment of compliant taxpayers, to sustain support for reform.

title: BOI zone leakage ‘immense’ as Customs move stalls: IMF | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:44
-     - 4

Customs control and oversight of Board of Investment (BOI) enterprises remains incomplete despite a 2025 agreement, leaving duty-exempt inputs open to diversion into the domestic market without payment of applicable taxes, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said, as tax exemptions and incentives, including BOI regimes, cost Sri Lanka close to Rs. 800 billion to Rs. 1 trillion annually in recent years.

Customs responsibilities for some 200 enterprises in special economic zones (SEZs) and 1,500 operating outside them have rested with the BOI rather than Sri Lanka Customs (SLC). “BOI did not carry out a full customs role, with no inspections and documentation being generally accepted as presented by the operator,” the IMF said in its Revenue Administration Diagnostic, adding that the BOI does not closely monitor the movement of goods, check inventory or enforce violations, leaving opportunities for revenue leakage it described as immense.

Under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed with the BOI in 2025, the initial phase of SLC control included 83 companies selected for scrutiny, but little progress has been made. “Many companies have expressed resistance to this change given the more intense oversight that will ensue,” the report said. SLC has sought additional staff and, for the time being, only imports will be checked, while a GPS tracking system is being procured with Asian Development Bank (ADB) support.

Granting SLC clear responsibility for import and export controls in the 12 BOI-administered SEZs is a commitment under the IMF program. Gaps in oversight also create unfair competition for compliant importers and domestic producers that pay applicable duties and taxes, the Fund said. “Any slowing or reversal after formalizing such commitments through the MOU would introduce uncertainty about the regulatory framework,” it warned.

At the border, aggregate physical examination rates remain high by international standards at close to 38%, down from 53% in 2021, though SLC’s internal risk-targeting framework accounts for about 16.3% of import containers, with the balance reflecting mandatory requirements of other government agencies. Examination success rates vary widely: 58.5% of examinations at grayline yards 1 and 2 resulted in findings in 2026, against 8.5% at the Rank Container Terminal and 7.3% for less-than-container-load cargo. “Examinations with no significant revenue result are an inefficient use of SLC resources, increase compliance costs for traders, and should trigger a review of risk criteria,” the IMF said.

Post-clearance audit (PCA), which checks declarations after goods are cleared, reported results of Rs. 4.6 billion in 2024, Rs. 2.48 billion in 2025 and Rs. 2.75 billion in the first five months of 2026, including additional entries, penalties and mitigated forfeitures, but the function is constrained by limited staffing, with four teams reviewing 304 blue-channel PCA shipments from January to March 2026. The Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) trusted-trader program, comprising 75 companies that represent close to 10% of trade volume, has been slow to take root, while uptake of paperless processing has been slowed by fear of job losses among brokers and concerns over the digital signature requirement. All importers are expected to be paperless by 1 January, 2027.

title: Sri Lanka Tourism funds Rs. 104.6 m for Asian Broadcasting Union General Assembly | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:43
-     - 5

Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau is sponsoring the 63rd Asian Broadcasting Union (ABU) General Assembly and associated meetings, music festival and excursion in Sri Lanka to the tune of Rs. 104.6 million following the approval of the Cabinet of Ministers.

The General Assembly and connected activities kicked off on Sunday in Colombo and will go on till today (3).

ABU is one of the largest professional broadcasting organisations in the Asia Pacific region, bringing together broadcasters and media organisations to facilitate cooperation, knowledge exchange and collaboration across broadcasting community. ABU comprises 225 members from 66 countries covering eight geographical regions - the Pacific, Southeast Asia, North Asia, South Asia, Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa and Northern America. The meetings and related program is hosted by MTV Channel Ltd.

SLTPB is sponsoring the initiative as participation of leading broadcasters and media organisations would further enhance the potential for international exposure of Sri Lanka as a tourism destinations. 

The proposal to this effect was submitted to the Cabinet by Foreign Affairs, Tourism and Foreign Employment Minister Vijitha Herath. MTV Channel has proposed the initiative as a strategic investment in tourism promotion, media diplomacy and nation branding for Sri Lanka.

The opening ceremony of the General Assembly on Sunday was graced by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake. Over 350 broadcasters, media leaders, industry experts, policymakers and partners from across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond have gathered for the event, on the theme ‘Media for Peace and Humanity: Truth, Trust and Transformation.’

title: SLTPB Chairman Buddhika Hewawasam resigns  | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:41
-     - 3

Buddhika Hewawasam

Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau (SLTPB) Chairman Buddhika Hewawasam has resigned following the completion of his two-year term, leaving the tourism promotion agency without an officially appointed successor or Acting Chairman as of yesterday.

Industry sources said Hewawasam’s final day in office was 30 October 2026, with no formal announcement on a replacement made by the time of reporting.

The Daily FT attempted to contact Hewawasam for comment, but he could not be reached.

His resignation comes as Sri Lanka Tourism rolls out its long-awaited interim, market-specific promotional campaigns to maintain the destination’s visibility in key international markets ahead of the winter travel season. These initiatives are expected to bridge the gap until the planned Rs. 3.5 billion global destination branding campaign, targeted for early 2027 (https://www.ft.lk/top-story/Rs-1-5-b-interim-tourism-campaign-kicks-off-ahead-of-global-brand-push/26-796239). 

Hewawasam had earlier resigned as Chairman of the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) on 17 August, citing personal and professional reasons (https://www.ft.lk/front-page/Hewawasam-resigns-as-SLTDA-Chairman/44-796136). Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath subsequently appointed Suranjith Wevita as the new SLTDA Chairman.

In October 2024, the Government introduced a dual-chairmanship arrangement under which Hewawasam headed both the SLTDA and SLTPB (https://www.ft.lk/front-page/Sri-Lanka-Tourism-gets-professionals-as-new-heads/44-767651). 

Before joining Sri Lanka Tourism, Hewawasam was an aviation and travel industry professional and served as Sri Lanka Manager of the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

title: Seylan reports 9M PAT of Rs. 9.1 b | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:40
-     - 3

Chairman Justice Buwaneka Aluwihare, PC (left) and Director/CEO Ramesh Jayasekara

Seylan Bank yesterday said it posted a Profit Before Tax (PBT) of Rs. 14.04 million 3Q 2026, compared with Rs. 12.8 million in 3Q 2025, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 9.64%.

For the nine months ended 30 September 2026, the bank recorded a Profit After Tax (PAT) of Rs. 9.12 billion, an increase of 9.47% from Rs. 8.33 billion reported in the corresponding period of 2025.

Net Interest Income increased by 6.62% to Rs. 28.8 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, compared with Rs. 27 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. This growth was primarily driven by the significant expansion in the bank’s total assets over the year aptly supported by strong deposit mobilisation. However, the bank’s Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined from 4.5% in 2025 to 3.99% in 3Q 2026, due to the upward movement in market interest rates.

The bank’s net fee-based income recorded a growth of 18.19%, increasing to Rs. 7.1 billion in 3Q 2026 from Rs. 6 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. This growth was mainly attributable to increased fee income from cards, remittances, trade, loans and other financial services.

The bank’s total operating income increased by 8.87% to Rs. 37.2 billion in 3Q 2026, compared with last year’s Rs. 34.2 billion. This growth was primarily driven by increases in net interest income, net fee and commission income, net gains from derecognition of financial assets, and other operating income.

Total operating expenses increased by 13.54% to Rs. 18.6 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, compared with Rs. 16.3 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. Personnel expenses increased by 12.98%, from Rs. 8.7 billion to Rs. 9.9 billion, mainly due to annual salary revision. Other operating expenses including depreciation and amortisation expenses increased by 14.2%, reflecting higher prices of consumables and other related cost of services during the period. The bank continues to implement targeted cost optimisation initiatives to manage overhead cost effectively.

The bank recorded a net impairment reversal of Rs. 232 million in 3Q 2026, compared with a charge of Rs. 645 million reported in 3Q 2025. The bank continues to ensure that impairment provisions adequately reflect changes in global and domestic economic conditions, the credit risk profiles of customers, and credit quality of its loan portfolio. These measures are aimed at maintaining the adequacy of provisions recognised in the financial statements. The bank’s asset quality indicators remained stable, with the Impaired Loan (Stage 3) Ratio at 1.02% as at 30 September 2026, compared with 1.03% in December 2025. Meanwhile, the Stage 3 Provision Coverage Ratio stood at 84.98%, reflecting the bank’s Strong provision coverage.

Income tax expenses increased by 9.96% to Rs. 4.9 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, compared with Rs. 4.5 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Value Added Tax on Financial Services and the Social Security Contribution Levy increased by 10.53%, from Rs. 4.4 billion to Rs. 4.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026.

During the period the bank’s total assets surpassed the one trillion mark and increased to Rs. 1.01 trillion from Rs. 921 billion reported in 2025. Seylan Bank became the fourth private commercial bank in Sri Lanka to reach this milestone. The bank continues to attract new customers for loans and deposits, while strengthening relationships with its existing customer base.

Loans and advances recorded a net growth of Rs. 89 billion, reaching Rs. 689 billion, while customer deposits increased by Rs. 78 billion to Rs. 811 billion during the first nine months of 2026. The bank’s CASA ratio stood at 26%.

Key financial ratios and indicators of Seylan Bank PLC remained sound as at 30 September 2026. The bank maintained capital adequacy ratios well above the regulatory minimum requirements, with both the Common Equity Tier 1 Capital Ratio and the Total Tier 1 Capital Ratio standing at 11.12%, while the Total Capital Ratio stood at 15.14%.

The bank’s liquidity position remained strong, with the All Currency Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) and the Rupee LCR recorded at 163.01% and 171.69%, respectively, both well above the minimum statutory requirements.

The bank’s asset quality indicators remained strong, with Impaired Loan (Stage 3) Ratio standing at 1.02%, compared with 1.03% in 2025. The Stage 3 Impairment Provision Coverage Ratio stood at 84.98%, one of the highest in the banking industry.

The Return on Equity (ROE) stood at 14.44%, compared with 15.89% in 2025, while the Return on Average Assets (before tax) was 1.94%, compared with 2.31% in the corresponding period.

The bank’s Earnings per Share (EPS) increased to Rs. 14.34 in 3Q 2026, compared with Rs. 13.10 recorded in 3Q 2025. As at 30 September 2026, the Net Asset Value per Share stood at Rs. 136.68 for the bank and Rs. 140.09 for the group.

The National Long Term Rating of Seylan Bank, was upgraded by two notches, to A+(lka) with a Stable Outlook by Fitch Ratings in 2025.

title: Low Grown lifts Oct., tea average to 2026 high | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:39
-     - 3

The national tea sale average climbed to its highest monthly level so far this year in October, lifted by Low Grown teas, but the average in US dollars fell from a year earlier as the rupee weakened against the dollar.

The national sale average for October 2026 was Rs. 1,217.46 a kilo, Rs. 40.32 or 3.43% higher than October 2025 and Rs. 14.72 above September 2026, John Keells PLC said in its Market Insights report on National Tea Sale Averages, issued on Saturday. The report is based on Sri Lanka Tea Board data and Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) exchange rates.

Low Grown teas drove the increase. Their average rose by Rs. 67.08 or 5.44% to Rs. 1,299.26 a kilo. The High Grown average fell 1.14% to Rs. 1,134.13 and the Medium Grown average dropped 2.50% to Rs. 1,005.23. Low Grown teas also made up a larger share of the tea sold, at 63.27% against 60.56% in October 2025. According to the report, that change in mix accounts for about Rs. 4.75 of the Rs. 40.32 increase in the national average.

The gains did not hold in dollar terms. The national average was $ 3.67 a kilo, down $ 0.21 or 5.41% from October 2025 and down $ 0.32 or 8.02% from October 2024. Every elevation average was lower in US dollars than a year earlier. Over the same period, the rupee depreciated by 8.54% against the dollar, from Rs. 303.13 to Rs. 331.42, based on CBSL average rates. Compared with September 2026, the dollar average rose by $ 0.02 or 0.55% from $ 3.65.

Within the elevations, the regions moved in opposite directions. The Uva High average rose 3.25% to Rs. 1,095.57 a kilo and Uva Medium gained 2.72% to Rs. 1,100.73. In contrast, Western High fell 1.69% to Rs. 1,187.44 and Western Medium dropped 4.92% to Rs. 976.55. Green tea averaged Rs. 1,291.01, up 2.38%.

The method of manufacture produced an even sharper split. Orthodox teas, made by the traditional process of rolling the leaf, averaged Rs. 1,274.92 a kilo, up 5.04%. Low Grown orthodox led with Rs. 1,345.17, Rs. 79.67 or 6.30% higher. CTC teas, machine-processed by the crush, tear and curl method into small granules mostly used in tea bags, averaged Rs. 946.74, down 7.17%. The CTC average fell at every elevation: 6.41% at High Grown to Rs. 1,064.37, 8.33% at Medium Grown to Rs. 894.34 and 7.18% at Low Grown to Rs. 936.83.

Volumes sold in October totalled 19.13 MnKg, down 1.51% from 19.43 MnKg. Medium Grown fell the most, down 12.49% to 3.14 MnKg, and High Grown declined 4.53% to 3.89 MnKg. Low Grown rose 2.90% to 12.11 MnKg.

For the first 10 months, the national average was Rs. 1,174.47 a kilo, up Rs. 12.48 or 1.07% from Rs. 1,161.99 in January to October 2025, but below Rs. 1,236.92 for the same period of 2024. The High Grown average rose 1.69% to Rs. 1,107.70 and Low Grown increased 1.92% to Rs. 1,254.71. Medium Grown was the only one of the three main elevations with a lower average, down 4.25% to Rs. 979.89. The report added that every elevation average is still below January to October 2024.

The year-to-date regional pattern is the reverse of October’s. Western High rose 3.63% to Rs. 1,168.03 a kilo while Uva High slipped 0.49% to Rs. 1,045.84. Western Medium fell the most, by 5.64% to Rs. 954.94.

In dollar terms, the January to October average was $ 3.63 a kilo, down $ 0.25 or 6.44% from a year earlier, while the rupee depreciated 7.47%, from Rs. 299.47 to Rs. 323.66 per dollar.

The orthodox average for the period rose 1.76% to Rs. 1,219.86 a kilo, while CTC fell 4.32% to Rs. 944.24, lower at High, Medium and Low Grown. title: October tourist arrivals hit all-time monthly high | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:38
-     - 4

Sri Lanka recorded its highest-ever monthly tourist arrivals in October, welcoming 168,625 visitors as demand strengthened ahead of the winter season, although the increase in visitor numbers has yet to translate into higher tourism earnings.

The latest figures released by the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) show October arrivals surpassing the previous monthly record of 165,193 set in 2025, marking a 2.08% year-on-year (YoY) increase.

The performance lifted cumulative arrivals during the first 10 months of 2026 to over 1.86 million, although the total remained 1.5% below the corresponding period last year.

The October recovery is particularly significant given the disruption to international travel caused by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which have affected long-haul air traffic from Europe and contributed to higher travel costs across several markets.

However, industry stakeholders remain cautious about the record arrivals, pointing to the continuing weakness in tourism receipts, which are a more significant measure of the sector’s contribution to foreign exchange earnings and the wider economy.

India provided the strongest impetus to October’s performance, with arrivals from the market rising 19.79% month-on-month to 62,211, accounting for 37% of total visitors. This was the highest monthly contribution from India so far in 2026, surpassing the previous peaks of 60,342 in May and 52,062 in January.

The UK followed with 12,402 visitors, representing 7% of arrivals, while China contributed 11,190 (7%), Australia 8,509 (5%) and Germany 8,027 (5%). Russia, France, Bangladesh, the US and the Maldives were among the other significant source markets.

Sri Lanka registered an average of 5,440 arrivals per day in October, compared with 5,329 during the same period last year. The highest daily influx was 7,045 visitors on 17 October.

India continued to consolidate its position as Sri Lanka’s largest source market during the first 10 months, contributing 499,625 visitors, or 27% of total arrivals. This represented an increase of 76,220 Indian travellers compared with the corresponding period last year.

The UK ranked second with 173,129 visitors , followed by China with 123,740, Germany with 105,305 and Australia with 95,498.

Although arrivals from India and Australia registered growth, the UK and Germany remained below their corresponding year-earlier levels. China, meanwhile, posted an improvement against the previous year’s comparable period. 

The latest October performance comes against a more challenging outlook for the full year, following the SLTDA’s downward revision of its 2026 arrival projections in early September amid the continuing Middle East conflict, higher energy costs and uncertainty surrounding international travel.

Under the revised scenarios, full-year arrivals are projected to range between 2,377,370 and 2,603,311, depending on how external conditions evolve during the remaining months.

The lower-end projection would place arrivals only marginally above the 2025 record, while the upper scenario of around 2.6 million would still fall short of the original three million target by nearly 400,000 visitors.

title: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1’s youngest world champion in Mexico City | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:34
-     - 1

Red Bull Racing’s Max Verstappen holds the trophy on the podium next to second-placed Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton and third-placed Mercedes’s Kimi Antonelli at the Mexico City Formula One Grand Prix

Kimi Antonelli has become Formula One’s youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old with his third-place finish for Mercedes at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The first Italian champion since 1953 sobbed with joy over the team radio as he took the chequered flag at the high-altitude Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won the red-flagged, restarted race for his second win of the season, but Antonelli’s overall lead reached an unassailable 119 points after finishing third.

Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton started from pole position and took a close second place – after clashing with teammate Charles Leclerc – on an afternoon of drama, with two safety cars, multiple crashes and an agonising 33-minute halt with 25 of the 71 laps remaining.

“Get in there, Kimi. Champion of the world,” said his race engineer Peter Bonnington, a regular target for the young driver’s practical jokes.

“We did it. Thank you so much,” gasped the Italian, whose parents and sister were there to embrace him when he stepped out of the car. He was then mobbed by his pit crew.

The previous youngest champion was Germany’s Sebastian Vettel, who took the first of his four with Red Bull at 23 years and 134 days old in 2010.

The last Italian champion was Alberto Ascari, 73 years earlier. “On the last lap, I just backed off, because I just couldn’t see the track. I was getting emotional,” Antonelli told a later news conference. “So it was just good to bring it home.”

Leclerc finished fourth, McLaren’s outgoing champion Lando Norris fifth, and Antonelli’s teammate George Russell only sixth in a race he had to win to have any chance of staying in contention.

That also meant that Verstappen went second in the overall standings, with Hamilton third and preseason favourite Russell plummeting to fourth, 130 points behind Antonelli.

Mercedes have 630 points in the constructors’ standings to Ferrari’s 504 and could clinch that title in Brazil next weekend.

The race was stopped after a brief safety car deployment on lap 46 of 71 after Valtteri Bottas suffered a high-speed front-left suspension failure down the straight, with his Cadillac pitching uncontrollably into the barriers at turn one.

Bottas received medical attention in the car, but then walked to an ambulance, giving a thumbs-up, as the rest of the field returned to the pits. He went to the medical centre and was released.

Verstappen led from the restart, challenged by Hamilton, with Antonelli passing Leclerc. There was then another safety car when Lindblad and Piastri collided, with the field released to race again with nine laps to the chequered flag.

Hamilton had led away from the original pole position for the 105th time in his career, but the first for Ferrari at a full Grand Prix, with Leclerc slotting in behind from third on the grid.

The British driver held him off as they went side by side through the opening corners, but Leclerc cut turn four and went across the grass as they battled for the lead, with Verstappen then taking second from Hamilton as the Ferrari looped wide.

“Pushed out by ‌my own teammate,” Hamilton said over the radio.

The stewards handed Leclerc a five-second penalty, but that did little for Hamilton, who remained behind his teammate after their respective stops on laps 28 and 29, with the Monegasque taking his penalty.

Russell, who had lined up on the front row, made a poor start and dropped to fifth. He also collided with Hadjar, punting the Red Bull off, and the stewards handed him a 10-second penalty.

Afghanistan have climbed to the sixth spot in the ICC Men’s ODI Team Rankings, surpassing Sri Lanka to secure their highest-ever position.

Over 250 international women have arrived in Sri Lanka for the globally recognised adventure challenge Raid Amazones 2026, which began yesterday in Kalutara.

The contingent included competitors event organisers, media representatives and medical personnel. The 2026 Raid Amazones will be conducted until 10 November bringing international attention to the country’s adventure tourism potential, natural landscapes and distinctive hospitality.

Founded in 2001 by French adventure event specialist Alexandre Debanne, Raid Amazones is an internationally recognised women-only adventure challenge that combines physical endurance, teamwork and outdoor exploration with cultural discovery. The event encourages women to step beyond their comfort zones, build connections and experience destinations through meaningful interactions with local communities.

Returning to Sri Lanka for its eighth edition, the event will take participants through the diverse landscapes of Kalutara, including its coastline, rivers, wetlands, tropical vegetation and rural communities. Beyond the adventure activities, participants will have opportunities to discover Sri Lankan traditions, cuisine and the warmth of local hospitality.

Connaissance de Ceylan, one of Sri Lanka’s leading destination management companies, is serving as the official ground handling partner for Raid Amazones Sri Lanka 2026. The company is coordinating local ground operations, transfers and logistical arrangements, working closely with the international organising team and relevant stakeholders to ensure a seamless experience for the visiting participants and delegation.

Connaissance de Ceylan Director – Marketing and Business Development Maxime Wickramasinghe said: “Welcoming an international community of this scale is a wonderful opportunity to showcase what Sri Lanka has to offer. As the official ground handling partner, Connaissance de Ceylan is working closely with the Raid Amazones team to ensure that participants enjoy a smooth and memorable experience from the moment they arrive in the country. Beyond the operational aspects, we want every participant to experience our hospitality, discover our diverse landscapes and take home a genuine appreciation of Sri Lanka.” 

The event is being delivered through a collaborative partnership between Raid Amazones, SriLankan Airlines and Connaissance de Ceylan, with the support of the Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau. Turyaa Kalutara serves as the official accommodation partner, hosting participants and the international delegation throughout the event.

Raid Amazones 2026 provides another valuable opportunity to showcase Sri Lanka as a destination where adventure, nature, culture and authentic experiences come together.

title: Pakistan penalised for slow over-rate in victory over Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 3 November 2026 03:32

Pakistan have been fined five per cent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during the Final of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday.

The hosts were found to be one over short after time allowances were taken into consideration by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees.

Their breach was in accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time.

On field umpires Ahsan Raza and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid, and fourth umpire Rashid Riaz levelled the charge.

Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pled guilty to the slow over-rate offence and accepted the proposed sanction.

Pakistan conceded 325/8 with the ball in the match, before chasing down the target by three wickets and nine balls to spare, taking away positives on the road to next year’s ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup. 

In front of their home fans in Lahore, Pakistan’s batting lineup delivered on all fronts, led by the experienced campaigner Fakhar Zaman. 

The left-handed batter scored his 12th ODI century, belting 127 off 99 deliveries, which included 11 fours and six sixes.

The Sri Lanka National football contingent team before the departure for the 15th SAFF Football Tournament to be held in Dhaka, Bangladesh from 5 to 17 November

By Althaf Nawaz

 The National Football team left for Dhaka, Bangladesh yesterday to take part in the 15th Edition of the SAFF Football Tournament to be held in a single venue at the National Stadium Dhaka from 5 to 17 November.

The 30 strong Sri Lankan contingent comprised the players, officials and support staff.  

South Asia›s biggest football extravaganza - tagged as the ‘World Cup’ for South Asian countries - will see the participation of six major countries - Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India, Pakistan, Maldives and hosts Bangladesh respectively.

Head coach Abdullah Al Mutairi speaking to Daily FT was very optimistic over his players performance in the recent past, where a couple of wins in the friendly international encounters has given them the much-needed impetus to surge into this tournament with confidence. Sri Lanka annexed this championship way back in 1995 in Colombo under the leadership of Sampath Perera.

«As a unit we were able to play friendly encounters in Seychelles and Mauritius. These matches enabled us to identify our shortcomings and gave the much-needed exposure for the boys to jell as a unit. We always like to concentrate match by match and move forward step by step without rushing. We have evaluated the participating teams’ strengths and weaknesses and will execute our plans at the right time,» said Al Mutairi 

The Lankans – now placed 184th in the FIFA rankings - will play their curtain raiser on the 8th against Bhutan and then will lock horns against hosts Bangladesh, before moving to the semi-final (14th) and the Grand Finale on the 17th at the same venue.

Defending champions India have won this tournament on 9 occasions and Maldives on 2 occasions, while Sri Lanka, Afghanistan and Bangladesh have managed to win on a single occasion.

The National team has played over 30 matches in the past 3 years, which was due the indefatigable efforts of incumbent President Jaswar Umar.

Jaswar, who is also the AFC Tournament Committee Chairman, speaking to Daily FT said: «The boys left for Bangladesh with a good temperament. We have strived hard in the recent past to give them much needed match exposure. Now the team is well set and we expect them to deliver the goods for their country.»

«We will focus match by match and want to make sure that we first win our group games to secure a place in the semis, and then to qualify for the grand final on 17 November to win this Championship,» added Jaswar.
